citation.note: Wage reduction notice (Idaho Code § 45-610): Employers must inform employees of any wage reductions before the affected work is performed; written notice required if requested by employee.

Three-year record retention: Idaho Code § 45-610 requires employers maintain employment records for 3 years from date of separation; must provide wage information and notice of wage reductions to employees.

Idaho Code § 45-606 does not mandate a specific pay frequency (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly); employers may set frequency by agreement, but must pay consistently and in accordance with wage payment rules.

Final pay timing strict (10 days or regular payday): Idaho Code § 45-606 requires wages by the earlier of the next regular payday or 10 days after termination; employee request for early payment triggers 48-hour deadline (weekends/holidays excluded).

body.deadline_description: Final pay timing strict (10 days or regular payday): Idaho Code § 45-606 requires wages by the earlier of the next regular payday or 10 days after termination; employee request for early payment triggers 48-hour deadline (weekends/holidays excluded).

citation.note: Non-competes enforceable with limits: Idaho Code §§ 44-2701, 44-2704 enforce non-competes for "key employees" only if reasonable in duration (18 months max, presumed reasonable if ≤18 months), geography, and scope; must protect legitimate business interests.

body.rule: Non-competes enforceable with limits: Idaho Code §§ 44-2701, 44-2704 enforce non-competes for "key employees" only if reasonable in duration (18 months max, presumed reasonable if ≤18 months), geography, and scope; must protect legitimate business interests.

citation.note: Wage deductions restricted: Deductions only permitted if required by law or with written employee authorization (Idaho Code § 45-609); must provide itemized statement of deductions; unpaid wages accrue 15-day penalty (up to $750).

citation.note: Public policy exception: Termination in violation of established public policy (e.g., retaliation for filing a workers' compensation claim, fulfilling jury duty, or reporting illegal activity) may create liability.

citation.note: No state-level statute regulating private-sector drug testing: Idaho does not restrict private employers' ability to conduct pre-employment, reasonable-suspicion, or post-accident drug testing.
Data breach notification required: Idaho Code § 28-51-105 mandates notification "without unreasonable delay" if personal data accessed/misused; state agencies must notify AG within 24 hours.

Minimum wage tracks federal: Idaho Code § 44-1502 sets minimum wage at $7.25 per hour and automatically adjusts when federal minimum wage changes; reduced $4.25 per hour for employees under 20 in their first 90 days; tipped minimum $3.35 per hour in direct wages with make-up to the minimum.
